## Overview

`llama-modchip` is a set of `ggml`/`llama.cpp` kernel patches, quantization transcoders, and runtime tools designed to run sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) checkpoints entirely in system RAM on x86_64 (`AVX-512` / `AVX2`) and ARM64 (`NEON` / `SVE` / Apple Metal) processors:

1. **Fitting 284B `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` into 64 GB Physical RAM (`56.56 GiB` on disk, `1.71 bpw`):** Standard `UD-IQ1_S` builds of `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (`284.33B` total, `13.17B` active across 43 MLA layers and 256 routed experts) occupy `76.87 GiB` (`82.5 GB`), exceeding the ~62.5 GiB of usable RAM on a 64 GB Linux system and causing page-cache thrashing or OOM kills. `llama-modchip` reduces the checkpoint to `56.56 GiB` (`60.73 GB`) so the entire model plus a `256K` KV cache (`57.61–58.9 GiB` `VmRSS`) locks into RAM with zero swap. By default, all 6 routed experts per layer (`Top-6`) are evaluated without pruning.
2. **CPU Cache & SIMD Kernel Patches (`+77%` prefill, `+53%` decode):** Replaces single-column quantized matrix-vector loops during prompt prefill with a 4-level register (`ZMM` AVX-512BW) + L1D (`32 KB`) + L2 (`1 MB`) + L3 (`64 MB`) multi-column (`{8,4,3,2}`) tiling schedule (`25.0 -> 44.36 tok/s` on 16-core Zen 5), register-stationary `MQA8` FlashAttention, and non-temporal `_MM_HINT_NTA` MoE streaming so cold expert weights do not evict hot KV cache lines from L3.
3. **Self-Speculative Drafting & Instant Agent Context Restore:** Pairs a `1.64 MB` L2/L3 Zobrist n-gram drafter (`Stockfish-PVS v2`) with `/dev/shm` KV slot snapshots (`13.1–32.6 ms` restore time for 40-tool Claude Code prompts) and an $O(1)$ speculative rollback fix for `deepseek4` recurrent/MLA states.

---

## Quantization & Memory Breakdown

To answer the most common technical question upfront—**exact bit-widths (`bpw`), base checkpoints, and what is compressed in each GGUF**:

| Checkpoint | Total / Active Params | Base Source | Disk Size (`GiB` / `GB`) | Effective `bpw` | Layer-by-Layer Tensor Allocation |
| :--- | :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **`Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B-Q4_0`** | `30.2B` / `3.0B` | BF16 Official | `17.59 GiB` (`18.89 GB`) | **`4.50 bpw`** | Standard `Q4_0` across MoE + attention; `F32` norms & SSM conv/decay |
| **`Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B-MXFP4`** | `30.2B` / `3.0B` | BF16 Official | `15.95 GiB` (`17.13 GB`) | **`4.25 bpw`** | `GGML_TYPE_MXFP4` (`E2M1` + shared exponent) on routed MoE; `Q4_0`/`Q8_0` trunk |
| **`Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B-Fractal-64`** | `30.2B` / `3.0B` | BF16 Official | `14.35 GiB` (`15.41 GB`) | **`3.75 bpw`** | Attention, Mamba-2 SSM & shared experts in `Q4_0`/`Q8_0`/`F32`; cold routed MoE experts in hybrid `Q4_0` + `Fractal-64` (`Q2_0`, 64-weight block + `BF16` scale). Scores `100/100` on [`benchmarks/eval_quality_and_tools.py`](benchmarks/eval_quality_and_tools.py). |
| **`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Fractal`** | `284.33B` / `13.17B` | Unsloth `UD-IQ1_S` (`76.87 GiB` / `82.5 GB`) | `56.56 GiB` (`60.73 GB`) | **`1.71 bpw`** | • **Embeddings, Dense L0, 43 Shared Experts (`shexp`), MLA `kv_a` / `q_a` / `wkv_b`:** Preserved in `Q4_K` / `Q5_K` / `F32`• **MLA `wq_b` & `attn_output` (`wo_a`/`wo_b`):** Transcoded to `Fractal-64` (`GGML_TYPE_Q2_0`, `3.75 bpw`, 30B/64-block w/ 8 sub-scales & `BF16` scale)• **256 Routed MoE Experts (`ffn_*_exps`):** Primarily `IQ1_S` (`1.5625 bpw`) with analytical `SwiGLU-H2` second-order scale matching; sensitive boundary layers preserved in `IQ2_XXS` (`2.06 bpw`) & `IQ1_M` (`1.75 bpw`) (`-20.31 GiB` vs `UD-IQ1_S`) |

> **Note on MoE Expert Routing (`Top-K`):** By default (`v2.4.0 Lossless`), `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` evaluates **all 6 routed experts + 1 shared expert (`Top-6`)** per layer with zero expert dropping (`1.00000` logit cosine similarity vs the unpatched runtime on the same checkpoint). Setting `LLAMA_MOE_TOP_K=5` or `4` is an optional runtime flag for users who want to trade a small perplexity delta for higher decode throughput.

---

## Quickstart

### Linux & macOS (Automated Setup & Chat)
```bash
git clone https://github.com/synchopate/llama-modchip.git
cd llama-modchip
./modchip chat
```

### Direct Run (Pre-Compiled Linux `x86_64` Binary + Hugging Face `.gguf`)
> **Compatibility Note (`GGML_TYPE_Q2_0 = 40`):** `Fractal-64` models use custom block-64 `BF16`-scale tensors (`GGML_TYPE_Q2_0`, type ID `40`) and `deepseek4` / `Stockfish-PVS` kernels. Unpatched `llama.cpp`, Ollama, or LM Studio binaries will reject them with `unknown tensor type 40`. Use `./modchip` above or the standalone pre-compiled binary (`llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64`, zero external `.so` dependencies) included in the Hugging Face repositories and [GitHub Release `v2.4.0`](https://github.com/synchopate/llama-modchip/releases/tag/v2.4.0):

```bash
# 1. For 30B Nemotron-3.5-A3B (14.35 GiB — runs in 16–32 GB RAM at 25–60.4 tok/s):
hf download Synchopate/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B-Fractal-64-CPU-GGUF \
  llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64 NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B-Fractal-64.gguf --local-dir .
chmod +x llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64
./llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64 -m NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B-Fractal-64.gguf -c 262144 -t 16 --port 8080

# 2. For 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash (56.56 GiB — fits in 64 GB RAM at 9.1–14.7 tok/s):
hf download Synchopate/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Fractal-64GB-CPU-GGUF --local-dir ./dsv4
chmod +x ./dsv4/llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64
./dsv4/llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64 -m ./dsv4/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Fractal-00001-of-00003.gguf -c 32768 -t 16 -fa on --port 8080
```

### Windows 10/11 (Hybrid GPU + CPU MoE Pack)
Open **[`windows/`](windows/README.md)** and run **[`windows/AVVIA_MODCHIP.bat`](windows/AVVIA_MODCHIP.bat)** (or `./modchip start` in Git Bash). It detects physical CPU cores, free RAM, and GPU VRAM (`nvidia-smi`), downloads `llama.cpp` CUDA 12.4 / Vulkan binaries, computes the `--n-cpu-moe` split, and launches the Web Chat UI (`http://127.0.0.1:8080`).

| `./modchip` Command | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`./modchip chat`** | Interactive terminal chat with live `tok/s`, TTFT, and `Stockfish-PVS` acceptance telemetry |
| **`./modchip web`** | Opens the Dark-Mode Web Chat & Live Telemetry HUD (`http://127.0.0.1:8787`) |
| **`./modchip bench`** | Runs a 30-second 2-stage speed test and prints a shareable CPU Benchmark Scorecard |
| **`./modchip claude`** | Launches Claude Code CLI (`40 tools`) wired to the local 256K engine (`18.9–32.6 ms` warm restore) |
| **`./modchip eval`** | Runs the reproducible 100-Point Quality, Tool-Calling, Coding & 8.5K Needle Gate |
| **`./modchip quantize`** | Transcodes `BF16`/`Q4_0`/`UD-IQ1_S` GGUFs into `Fractal-64` (`3.75 bpw`) or `Fractal-MXFP4` (`4.25 bpw`) |
| **`./modchip status` / `stop`** | Inspects CPU readiness, `2MB HugePages`, and `/dev/shm` IPC, or stops background services |

### Hardware Readiness Check (Zero Model Download Required)

```bash
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/synchopate/llama-modchip/main/scripts/check_cpu_readiness.py | python3
```

Submit your terminal scorecard via a [GitHub Benchmark Issue](https://github.com/synchopate/llama-modchip/issues/new?template=cpu_benchmark_submission.yml) or [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/synchopate/llama-modchip/discussions) to add your CPU to the leaderboard below.

## 📋 Overview

**MCP-Ollama Server** bridges the gap between Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) and local LLMs via Ollama. This integration empowers your on-premise AI models with Claude-like tool capabilities, including file system access, calendar integration, web browsing, email communication, GitHub interactions, and AI image generation—all while maintaining complete data privacy.

Unlike cloud-based AI solutions, MCP-Ollama Server:
- Keeps all data processing on your local infrastructure
- Eliminates the need to share sensitive information with third parties
- Provides a modular approach that allows you to use only the components you need
- Enables enterprise-grade AI capabilities in air-gapped or high-security environments

## ✨ Key Features

- **🔒 Complete Data Privacy**: All computations happen locally through Ollama
- **🔧 Tool Use for Local LLMs**: Extends Ollama models with file, calendar, and other capabilities
- **🧩 Modular Architecture**: Independent Python service modules that can be deployed selectively
- **🔌 Easy Integration**: Simple APIs to connect with existing applications
- **🚀 Performance Optimized**: Minimal overhead to maintain responsive AI interactions
- **📦 Containerized Deployment**: Docker support for each module (coming soon)
- **🧪 Extensive Testing**: Comprehensive test coverage for reliability

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.8+ installed
- [Ollama](https://ollama.ai/) set up on your system
- Git for cloning the repository

## 🧩 Component Overview

MCP-Ollama Server is organized into specialized modules, each providing specific functionality:

### 📅 Calendar Module

```
calendar/
├── README.md          # Module-specific documentation
├── google_calendar.py # Google Calendar API integration
├── pyproject.toml     # Dependencies and package info
└── uv.lock        # Dependency lock file
```

The Calendar module enables your local LLM to:
- Create, modify, and delete calendar events
- Check availability and scheduling conflicts
- Send meeting invitations
- Set reminders and notifications

### 🔄 Client MCP Module

```
client_mcp/
├── README.md      # Module-specific documentation
├── client.py      # Main client implementation
├── pyproject.toml # Dependencies and package info
├── testing.txt    # Test data
└── uv.lock        # Dependency lock file
```

The Client module provides:
- A unified interface to interact with all MCP-enabled services
- Conversation history management
- Context handling for improved responses
- Tool selection and routing logic

### 📁 File System Module

```
file_system/
├── README.md          # Module-specific documentation
├── file_system.py     # File system operations implementation
├── pyproject.toml     # Dependencies and package info
└── uv.lock            # Dependency lock file
```

The File System module allows your local LLM to:
- Read and write files securely
- List directory contents
- Search for files matching specific patterns
- Parse different file formats (text, CSV, JSON, etc.)

### Installation

```bash
# 1. First install uv if you haven't already
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# 2. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/sethuram2003/mcp-ollama_server.git
cd mcp-ollama_server

# 3. Verify Ollama model is installed (replace 'llama3' with your preferred model)
ollama pull llama3
```

### Module Configuration

1. **📅 Calendar Module:**

```bash
cd calendar
uv add pyproject.toml  # Install calendar-specific dependencies
```

2. **🔄 Client MCP Module:**

```bash
cd client_mcp
uv add pyproject.toml  # Install calendar-specific dependencies
```

3. **📁 File System Module:**

```python
cd file_system
uv add pyproject.toml  # Install filesystem dependencies
```
### Usage

## 🏗️ Architecture

MCP-Ollama Server follows a microservices architecture pattern, where each capability is implemented as an independent service:

### Key Components:

1. **Ollama Integration Layer**: Connects to your local Ollama instance and routes appropriate requests
2. **MCP Protocol Handlers**: Translate between standard MCP format and Ollama's requirements
3. **Service Modules**: Independent modules that implement specific capabilities
4. **Client Library**: Provides a unified interface for applications to interact with the system

This architecture provides several benefits:
- **Scalability**: Add new modules without affecting existing ones
- **Resilience**: System continues functioning even if individual modules fail
- **Flexibility**: Deploy only the components you need
- **Security**: Granular control over data access for each module

## ❓ FAQ

**Q: How does this differ from using cloud-based AI assistants?**  
A: MCP-Ollama Server runs entirely on your local infrastructure, ensuring complete data privacy and eliminating dependence on external APIs.

**Q: What models are supported?**  
A: Any model compatible with Ollama can be used. For best results, we recommend Llama 3, Mistral, or other recent open models with at least 7B parameters.

**Q: How can I extend the system with new capabilities?**  
A: Follow the modular architecture pattern to create new service modules. See our [Extension Guide](docs/extension.md) for details.

**Q: What are the system requirements?**  
A: Requirements depend on the Ollama model you choose. For basic functionality, we recommend at least 16GB RAM and a modern multi-core CPU.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
check_cpu_readiness.py — Hardware Compatibility & Performance Estimator
for Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B (256K Context, CPU-Only + RouteCrack Speculative Engine)

Zero-dependency Python 3 script (standard library only).
Inspects CPU topology, SIMD/AMX ISA extensions, L3 cache capacity, RAM,
Transparent HugePages (THP), runs a fast multi-core DRAM bandwidth micro-benchmark,
and estimates real-world latency (TTFT) and throughput (tok/s) for interactive
autonomous coding agents (e.g. Claude Code).

Usage:
    python3 scripts/check_cpu_readiness.py [--json] [--no-bench]
"""

import argparse
import ctypes
import ctypes.util
import glob
import json
import mmap
import multiprocessing
import os
import platform
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

# ============================================================================
# 1. System & CPU Topology Detection
# ============================================================================

def run_cmd(cmd):
    try:
        out = subprocess.check_output(cmd, shell=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=4)
        return out.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
    except Exception:
        return ""

def parse_size_to_mb(val_str):
    if not val_str:
        return 0.0
    m = re.search(r"([\d\.]+)\s*(KiB|MiB|GiB|KB|MB|GB|K|M|G)?", val_str, re.IGNORECASE)
    if not m:
        return 0.0
    num = float(m.group(1))
    unit = (m.group(2) or "B").upper()
    if unit.startswith("K"):
        return num / 1024.0
    if unit.startswith("M"):
        return num
    if unit.startswith("G"):
        return num * 1024.0
    return num / (1024.0 * 1024.0)

def detect_cpu_and_cache():
    info = {
        "os": platform.system(),
        "arch": platform.machine(),
        "model_name": platform.processor() or "Unknown CPU",
        "sockets": 1,
        "physical_cores": os.cpu_count() or 1,
        "logical_threads": os.cpu_count() or 1,
        "numa_nodes": 1,
        "l3_total_mb": 0.0,
        "l3_instances": 1,
        "flags": set(),
    }

    if info["os"] == "Linux":
        # Read /proc/cpuinfo
        try:
            with open("/proc/cpuinfo", "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                cpuinfo = f.read()
            for line in cpuinfo.splitlines():
                if line.startswith("model name") and info["model_name"] in ("Unknown CPU", "x86_64", ""):
                    info["model_name"] = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
                elif line.startswith("flags") or line.startswith("Features"):
                    flags_str = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip().lower()
                    info["flags"].update(flags_str.split())
        except Exception:
            pass

        # Parse lscpu for accurate physical cores, sockets, L3 cache, NUMA
        lscpu_out = run_cmd("LC_ALL=C lscpu")
        cores_per_socket = None
        sockets = 1
        hypervisor = None
        for line in lscpu_out.splitlines():
            if ":" not in line:
                continue
            k, v = [x.strip() for x in line.split(":", 1)]
            kl = k.lower()
            if kl == "model name":
                info["model_name"] = v
            elif kl == "hypervisor vendor":
                hypervisor = v
            elif kl == "socket(s)":
                try:
                    sockets = int(v)
                    info["sockets"] = sockets
                except ValueError:
                    pass
            elif kl == "core(s) per socket":
                try:
                    cores_per_socket = int(v)
                except ValueError:
                    pass
            elif kl == "cpu(s)":
                try:
                    info["logical_threads"] = int(v)
                except ValueError:
                    pass
            elif kl == "numa node(s)":
                try:
                    info["numa_nodes"] = int(v)
                except ValueError:
                    pass
            elif kl == "l3 cache":
                # e.g. "64 MiB (2 instances)"
                info["l3_total_mb"] = parse_size_to_mb(v)
                inst_m = re.search(r"\((\d+)\s+instance", v, re.IGNORECASE)
                if inst_m:
                    info["l3_instances"] = int(inst_m.group(1))

        if cores_per_socket:
            info["physical_cores"] = cores_per_socket * sockets

        # KVM/QEMU often exposes fake 16MB L3 per vCPU ("16 instances = 256 MiB")
        if hypervisor and info["l3_instances"] >= 8 and info["l3_total_mb"] / info["l3_instances"] == 16.0:
            info["l3_total_mb"] = 64.0
            info["l3_instances"] = 2
            info["hypervisor"] = hypervisor

        # Fallback L3 detection via sysfs if lscpu didn't report it
        if info["l3_total_mb"] <= 0:
            try:
                l3_sz = run_cmd("cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cache/index3/size")
                if l3_sz:
                    info["l3_total_mb"] = parse_size_to_mb(l3_sz)
            except Exception:
                pass

        # Enumerate exact non-SMT physical core IDs (1 logical CPU per physical package + core_id)
        core_map = {}
        for cpu_dir in sorted(glob.glob("/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu[0-9]*")):
            m = re.search(r"cpu(\d+)$", cpu_dir)
            if not m:
                continue
            cid_num = int(m.group(1))
            try:
                with open(os.path.join(cpu_dir, "topology/physical_package_id")) as f:
                    pkg = int(f.read().strip())
                with open(os.path.join(cpu_dir, "topology/core_id")) as f:
                    core_id = int(f.read().strip())
                key = (pkg, core_id)
                if key not in core_map or cid_num < core_map[key]:
                    core_map[key] = cid_num
            except Exception:
                pass
        if core_map:
            phys_ids = sorted(core_map.values())
            info["physical_core_ids"] = phys_ids
            info["physical_cores"] = len(phys_ids)
        else:
            info["physical_core_ids"] = list(range(info["physical_cores"]))

    elif info["os"] == "Darwin":
        model = run_cmd("sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string")
        if model:
            info["model_name"] = model
        pcores = run_cmd("sysctl -n hw.physicalcpu")
        lcores = run_cmd("sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu")
        if pcores.isdigit():
            info["physical_cores"] = int(pcores)
        if lcores.isdigit():
            info["logical_threads"] = int(lcores)
        l3 = run_cmd("sysctl -n hw.l3cachesize")
        if l3.isdigit() and int(l3) > 0:
            info["l3_total_mb"] = int(l3) / (1024.0 * 1024.0)
        else:
            # Apple Silicon SLC / L2 estimate
            l2 = run_cmd("sysctl -n hw.l2cachesize")
            if l2.isdigit() and int(l2) > 0:
                info["l3_total_mb"] = (int(l2) * 2) / (1024.0 * 1024.0)
        if info["arch"] == "arm64":
            info["flags"].update(["neon", "asimd", "dotprod", "apple_amx"])
        info["physical_core_ids"] = list(range(info["physical_cores"]))
    else:
        info["physical_core_ids"] = list(range(info["physical_cores"]))

    phys_ids = info.get("physical_core_ids", list(range(info["physical_cores"])))
    if phys_ids == list(range(len(phys_ids))):
        info["taskset_mask"] = f"0-{len(phys_ids) - 1}" if len(phys_ids) > 1 else "0"
    else:
        info["taskset_mask"] = ",".join(str(x) for x in phys_ids)

    return info

def detect_memory_and_thp():
    mem = {
        "total_gb": 0.0,
        "available_gb": 0.0,
        "thp_enabled": "unknown",
        "thp_defrag": "unknown",
        "shm_total_gb": 0.0,
    }
    if platform.system() == "Linux":
        try:
            with open("/proc/meminfo", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                for line in f:
                    if line.startswith("MemTotal:"):
                        mem["total_gb"] = int(line.split()[1]) / (1024.0 * 1024.0)
                    elif line.startswith("MemAvailable:"):
                        mem["available_gb"] = int(line.split()[1]) / (1024.0 * 1024.0)
        except Exception:
            pass

        try:
            with open("/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                s = f.read().strip()
                m = re.search(r"\[(\w+)\]", s)
                mem["thp_enabled"] = m.group(1) if m else s
        except Exception:
            pass

        try:
            with open("/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                s = f.read().strip()
                m = re.search(r"\[([^\]]+)\]", s)
                mem["thp_defrag"] = m.group(1) if m else s
        except Exception:
            pass

        try:
            st = os.statvfs("/dev/shm")
            mem["shm_total_gb"] = (st.f_blocks * st.f_frsize) / (1024.0 ** 3)
        except Exception:
            pass

        # Handle un-capped LXC / container cgroups that report 1 PiB (1048576 GiB) MemTotal
        if mem["total_gb"] > 65536.0:
            numa_kb = 0
            numa_free_kb = 0
            for npath in glob.glob("/sys/devices/system/node/node*/meminfo"):
                try:
                    with open(npath, "r", encoding="utf-8") as nf:
                        for nline in nf:
                            if "MemTotal:" in nline:
                                numa_kb += int(nline.split()[-2])
                            elif "MemFree:" in nline:
                                numa_free_kb += int(nline.split()[-2])
                except Exception:
                    pass
            if 0 < numa_kb < (65536 * 1024 * 1024):
                mem["total_gb"] = numa_kb / (1024.0 * 1024.0)
                mem["available_gb"] = min(mem["available_gb"], max(numa_free_kb / (1024.0 * 1024.0), mem["total_gb"] * 0.80))
            elif mem["shm_total_gb"] > 0.5:
                mem["total_gb"] = mem["shm_total_gb"] if mem["shm_total_gb"] >= 24.0 else mem["shm_total_gb"] * 2.0
                mem["available_gb"] = min(mem["available_gb"], mem["total_gb"] * 0.85)
    elif platform.system() == "Darwin":
        tot = run_cmd("sysctl -n hw.memsize")
        if tot.isdigit():
            mem["total_gb"] = int(tot) / (1024.0 ** 3)
            mem["available_gb"] = mem["total_gb"] * 0.75
        mem["thp_enabled"] = "macos_superpages"

    return mem

# ============================================================================
# 2. Multi-Core Sustained DRAM Read Bandwidth Micro-Benchmark (Zero-Dependency)
# ============================================================================

_BW_READY = None
_BW_START_EVT = None

def _bw_pool_init(ready_val, start_evt):
    global _BW_READY, _BW_START_EVT
    _BW_READY = ready_val
    _BW_START_EVT = start_evt

def _bw_worker(args):
    buf_mb, iters = args
    size = buf_mb * 1024 * 1024
    libc_name = ctypes.util.find_library("c")
    libc = ctypes.CDLL(libc_name) if libc_name else None

    # Allocate anonymous mmap buffer and fault all pages in BEFORE barrier
    src = mmap.mmap(-1, size)

    if libc:
        src_ptr = ctypes.addressof(ctypes.c_char.from_buffer(src))
        libc.memset.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_size_t]
        libc.memchr.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_size_t]
        libc.memchr.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
        libc.memset(src_ptr, 0x5A, size)
    else:
        src[:] = b"\x5a" * size

    if _BW_READY is not None:
        with _BW_READY.get_lock():
            _BW_READY.value += 1
    if _BW_START_EVT is not None:
        _BW_START_EVT.wait()

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    if libc:
        # Pure SIMD DRAM Read scan (AVX-512 / AVX2 / NEON in glibc memchr):
        # Avoids the 2:1 Infinity Fabric GMI3 write-throttling penalty on 2-CCD Ryzen CPUs
        for _ in range(iters):
            libc.memchr(src_ptr, 0xFF, size)
    else:
        for _ in range(iters):
            src.find(b"\xff")
    elapsed = time.pe
